key_catalyst: TSMC capex-driven semiconductor selloff with memory supercycle unwind (SanDisk -8%, SK Hynix -9%, Micron -8%) as 10-year yield spikes to 4.60% near cycle high
reasoning: Today's semiconductor rout is severe and broadening (TSMC -2% on capex-driven valuation fears, memory names -8% to -9%) while the 10-year yield escalated to 4.60%, just 2bp from the cycle high, directly compressing QQQ's duration-heavy multiples. Unlike the 7/13 rout that reversed on a soft CPI surprise, the disinflation catalysts are now behind us—today's soft PPI was shrugged off as strong claims data re-priced September hike odds back to 44%, leaving no scheduled macro savior. With the memory unwind only on day one and SK Hynix trading overnight in Asia plus unresolved Iran/Hormuz risk, overnight gap-down risk is material despite Apple's all-time-high cushioning the index.
